learningOutcomes.description: Compare large numbers up to 8 digits using place value charts (Indian and International systems).
Estimate sums, differences, products, and quotients by rounding off to nearest tens, hundreds, and thousands.
Understand and apply Roman numerals for standard values up to 100.
Identify predecessors and successors of whole numbers and represent them on the number line.
Apply properties of whole numbers: closure, commutativity, associativity, and distributivity of multiplication over addition.
Identify and extend patterns in whole numbers using dots and geometric arrangements.
Find factors and multiples of given numbers and distinguish between prime and composite numbers.
Apply divisibility tests for 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, and 11.
Calculate Highest Common Factor (HCF) and Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) to solve real-world word problems.
Identify and distinguish points, line segments, rays, intersecting lines, and parallel lines.
Classify curves into open, closed, simple curves, and identify interior and exterior regions.
Identify vertices, sides, diagonals, angles, and sectors of polygons, triangles, quadrilaterals, and circles.
Measure and compare angles using a protractor; classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex, and complete.
Classify triangles based on sides (equilateral, isosceles, scalene) and angles (acute, right, obtuse).
Identify properties of special quadrilaterals (rectangle, square, parallelogram, rhombus, trapezium) and 3D shapes (prism, pyramid, cone, cylinder, sphere).
Understand the concept of negative numbers and represent positive and negative integers on a number line.
Compare and order integers; compute absolute values.
Perform addition and subtraction of integers using the number line and algebraic rules.
Represent fractions as parts of a whole and plot them on a number line.
Identify, convert, and simplify proper, improper, mixed, and equivalent fractions.
Compare like and unlike fractions; perform addition and subtraction of fractions.
Understand tenths, hundredths, and thousandths place values and convert between fractions and decimals.
Compare decimals and apply them in measurement of money (rupees/paise), length (cm/m/km), and weight (g/kg).
Add and subtract decimal numbers in practical contexts.
Collect and organize data using tally marks and frequency tables.
Interpret and construct pictographs with appropriate scales.
Read, interpret, and draw horizontal and vertical bar graphs.
Understand perimeter as boundary length and calculate perimeters of rectangles, squares, and regular polygons.
Understand area as surface enclosed and calculate areas of rectangles and squares using standard unit squares and formulas.
Solve practical real-world word problems involving perimeter and area of rectangular fields and rooms.
Understand the concept of a variable through matchstick patterns and general rules.
Form algebraic expressions using variables and basic arithmetic operations.
Form simple linear equations and find solutions through trial and error method.
Understand ratio as comparison by division and express ratios in simplest form.
Understand proportion as equality of two ratios and verify proportion using extreme and middle terms.
Apply the unitary method to solve daily life problems.
Identify lines of symmetry in familiar 2D shapes, letters, and nature.
Construct circles of given radius, perpendicular lines, and perpendicular bisectors of line segments using ruler and compasses.
Construct angles of standard measures (60°, 90°, 120°, 45°) and construct angle bisectors.
